links.outcome: LLM accuracy under misleading context and challenged answers across multi-turn medical QA
links.effect: Accuracy dropped from 91.2% to as low as 13.5% for Claude Sonnet 4 in multi-turn settings. Models did reasonably well under shallow perturbations. Indirect, context-based interventions were often more harmful than direct suggestions.
links.quote: Using controlled interventions on the MedQA dataset, we evaluate five state-of-the-art LLMs and find that while models perform reasonably well under shallow perturbations, they exhibit severe vulnerabilities in multi-turn settings, with accuracy dropping from 91.2% to as low as 13.5% for Claude Sonnet 4.

unlisted_practices: Multi-turn robustness evaluation distinguishing shallow (misleading initial context) from deep (challenged answers) robustness
Compounding intervention analysis across repeated turns

screen.reason: The study evaluates the multi-turn robustness and vulnerabilities of medical LLMs using a benchmark (MedQA-Followup) with controlled perturbations, but does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
